LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 4.3.2 NON- FICTION: AUTOBIOGRAPHY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Fiction and Non- Fiction 4.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- Fiction 4.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why do people write autobiographies?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- Fiction 4.3.2 Non- Fiction: Autobiography together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner conducts research on the structure of an autobiography from online

and offline sources.

● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner speaks engagingly when brainstorming and

discussing the content of the autobiography.

Values:
● Peace: This is enhanced as the learner displays tolerance with peers when working jointly to summarise the structure

of the autobiography on a graphic organiser and displays in class.

● Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner takes up assigned tasks to achieve goals when conducting a reading

session to read an autobiography from Kenya.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is promoted as the learner interacts with autobiographies on Kenyan personalities and appreciates their

journeys through life.
